name: Okayama Station East
tagline: The transport hub, with the department stores and Omotecho
description: The commercial centre stretching east from the Shinkansen station along Momotaro-odori to the Omotecho covered arcades, holding the department stores, the tram line and most of the city's restaurants. Living here means the bullet train, the buses and the shopping are all within a few minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the Shinkansen and the arcades within a short walk
pros: Shinkansen to Osaka in under an hour from the doorstep
Covered arcades, department stores and restaurants throughout
Tram and all bus routes converge here
cons: The highest rents in the city
Busy and commercial rather than pleasant

name: Korakuen and the Castle District
tagline: Across the river by the great garden and the black castle
description: The area around the Asahi river where Korakuen, one of the three great gardens of Japan, faces the black-walled castle from an island in the stream. Residential streets, museums and riverside paths, quiet and green, with the tram a few minutes away and the centre a fifteen-minute walk.
bestFor: Stays that want the garden and the river as the daily walk
pros: Korakuen and the castle on the doorstep
Riverside paths for running and cycling
cons: Fifteen minutes to the station and shops

name: Tsushima and the University District
tagline: North of the centre, where Okayama University sits
description: The northern district built around Okayama University's main campus, with student housing, cheap restaurants, bookshops and a flat cycling grid. Rents are lower than the centre and the cycle in takes about fifteen minutes, which is how most of the neighbourhood travels.
bestFor: Budget stays with a bike, near the university and cheap eating
cons: Fifteen minutes by bike to the station

name: Kurashiki Bikan
tagline: The preserved canal quarter twenty minutes down the line
description: A separate city fifteen minutes away by train, whose Bikan historical quarter is a preserved Edo-period merchant district of white-walled warehouses along a willow-lined canal, with the Ohara Museum, Japan's first Western art collection, in the middle of it. Rents are lower and the setting is far prettier.
bestFor: Stays that want the prettiest streets in the region and a short train in
pros: The preserved canal quarter and the Ohara Museum
Trains to Okayama every few minutes
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes by train to Okayama
Very busy with day visitors in the Bikan quarter

name: Higashiyama and the Southeast
tagline: Along the tram line east, residential and cheap
description: The residential districts following the tram line east from the centre towards Higashiyama, with ordinary apartment buildings, supermarkets, local restaurants and a settled population. It has no sights at all, which is exactly why the rents are the lowest within easy reach of the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting normal Japanese neighbourhood life at the lowest cost
pros: The lowest rents on the tram network
Direct tram into the centre in ten minutes
cons: Nothing to see or do locally
